name: structured listing continuation
mechanism: Nearly every position is a highly predictable token inside directory-style listing structure (newlines ending entry lines, map-grid digits, boilerplate like GOOGLE MAP, second halves of familiar names); early MLPs m0/m2/m3 and a4 appear to supply the local template/format recognition that makes these tokens forced.

name: completing multi-token list items
mechanism: Positions are the continuation of an item begun on the same listing line: word-piece suffixes (Enter->tainment, GOOG->LE, Bletch->ley), the second word of known place names, and digits finishing grid references or populations; m0/m3 PCA directions seem to carry the identity of the partially written item.

name: word-suffix and grid-digit completion
mechanism: The marked token finishes a split word or coordinate: place-name suffixes (Chiche->ster, Rams->gate, Hind->head), heading words (S->ights, Enter->tainment), and the digit right after a map-grid letter or population comma; early-layer m0 directions look like subword-continuation features.

name: second word of proper names
mechanism: Most positions are the whole second word of a familiar two-word name in an index line (Jewel Tower, Clarence House, Guards Museum, Hoxton Hotel) plus a few grid digits after a letter; m0/m3 directions appear to encode the memorized name so its second token is retrieved.

name: listing-formula slot tokens
mechanism: A grab-bag of formulaic slots in the guidebook listing template: all-caps category labels (CA->FE, OFF->ICE, CLOTH->ING), 'mains' after a price semicolon, 'dusk' after '7am-', closing punctuation and suffix completions; the m0 directions seem to be generic template-position features rather than one crisp function.

name: newline ending index lines
mechanism: The dominant pattern is the newline token that terminates an index/listing line (after a grid reference, category label, or heading), with a few name-suffix completions mixed in; m2/m3 directions and head 4.8 appear to detect that the current listing line is complete.

name: copying previously seen items
mechanism: Positions complete an item that already occurred earlier in the context or is stock vocabulary (repeated section headings like Activities/Sights, all-caps labels like COCKTAIL BAR, FERRY, recurring place names); the probes are four layer-4 attention heads, consistent with induction-style copying of the earlier occurrence.

name: heading-to-body newline transition
mechanism: Mostly the single newline right after a section heading or category label, before body text or the next numbered entry, plus a few one-letter icon/glyph tokens in listing formulas; late MLPs m11-m14 handle this late-context structural prediction.

name: template whitespace separators
mechanism: The affected tokens are whitespace: the newline ending a heading/label line and the bare space tokens inside the '(  MAP' / ';  h' listing templates; m11-m13 directions appear to track exact position within these rigid templates to emit the right separator.

name: single newline after headings
mechanism: Almost every position is the lone newline that closes a heading or category-label line (Sights, CLUB, CAFE, Pop 90,300) before the body text starts; m11-m13 directions look like a 'heading line just ended' feature choosing single over double newline.

name: separators before station and date anchors
mechanism: Positions are the predictable filler right before a fixed anchor: the space or ' t' (tube symbol) preceding a station name in hours/transport strings, and prepositions/articles before years ('in 1066', 'the 19th'); m11-m13 directions seem to anticipate the upcoming anchor type.

name: GOOGLE MAP boilerplate completion
mechanism: Dominated by the 'LE' token completing 'GOOG->LE' inside the '(  GOOGLE MAP )' boilerplate, with a few heading newlines mixed in; m11/m13 directions appear to recognize this exact recurring template string.

name: map-template symbol tokens
mechanism: Tokens at various fixed slots of the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' and hours/price templates: the opening paren, the ' G' starting GOOGLE, tube 't' and 'mains' symbols, and line-ending newlines; m12/m13 directions look like positional features within these boilerplate strings.

name: index entry name and line completion
mechanism: Positions complete an index/heading entry: the second word of a known name (Jewel Tower, Gat->wick, East->bourne, S->ights, CL->UB) or the newline ending a grid-referenced line; m14 and m12 directions appear to finish memorized entry names and close their lines.

name: slot fillers in address templates
mechanism: A mixed set of informative slot tokens inside rigid formulas: postcode digits after WC, street numbers after a semicolon, the next heading in a stock sequence (Shopping -> Information), name completions, and heading newlines; the shared function seems to be filling the content slot of a memorized template, but the set is heterogeneous.

name: MAP token in map boilerplate
mechanism: Almost every position is the ' MAP' token immediately after '(  ' in the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' boilerplate that follows a listing's category label; m14/m12 directions clearly encode this one recurring template continuation.

name: tokens following MAP in boilerplate
mechanism: Positions are the next step of the same map boilerplate (the space after ' MAP' before GOOGLE) plus similar formula tokens elsewhere ('am' after an opening hour digit, tube 't' after a semicolon, street numbers); m12/m14 directions again track position inside these fixed listing formulas.
